_comment: Which versions of this repository are actually archived, and under which DOI.
CITATION.cff carries a `version` and a `doi`, and together they assert that the identifier
names that version. On 2026-08-29 they asserted version 1.0.1 while Zenodo held only 1.0.0:
the version had been bumped in preparation for a deposit that was then correctly not made,
and the citation file went on claiming it. The test that guards CITATION.cff passed, because
it checked only that a git tag of that name existed -- which it did. A tag is not a deposit.
This file is the offline record of what has been deposited. A version may appear in
CITATION.cff only if it appears here. Adding a row is part of cutting a release, after the
Zenodo record exists and its DOI resolves, not before.

versions.verified: downloaded and compared file by file against `git archive v1.0.0`: 886 files, every SHA-256 equal

tagged_but_not_deposited.why: the intended next deposit. v1.0.2 was tagged for it and never deposited, and 13 numbered corrections have been appended since, 45 through 57. A count of the commits between the two tags is deliberately not given here: it depends on where the tag lands, the tag lands after this sentence is written, and it was written wrong twice before this line said so. `git rev-list --count v1.0.2..v1.0.3` answers it without drifting. Correction 57 is the one that matters for a deposit -- it withdrew the negative rejection-cost claim from Phase A and Phase KV, so archiving v1.0.2 would freeze a reading this study no longer makes. A tag can be deleted and a Zenodo record cannot, so the two steps are kept apart on purpose and this row moves to `versions` only once the DOI resolves.

tagged as the intended deposit on 2026-08-31 and superseded before one was made. Everything v1.0.1 was rejected for is fixed and recorded in Correction 43. The tag is kept rather than deleted, for the same reason v1.0.1's is: it is the record of a state this repository stood behind at the time.

signed and pushed, then an external review found seven correctness blockers in it, listed here as the commit that recorded them states them: a README saying both 0 and 2 incidents for Phase B, with the stale mechanism report behind a bolded causal claim inside that same failure; censoring compared across different populations; a coverage simulation calibrating a different estimand than the headline uses; token fork positions computed as characters over a whole-output average; an energy argument that was mathematically wrong; cost coefficients that confounded the drafter with the source tree; and a reproduction script that did not reproduce. An earlier version of this field called the first one a contradiction over coverage figures, which is a different defect, and dropped the fork positions while splitting the first in two to still reach seven. Not deposited. The next deposit is v1.0.2.
not a release; it is the harness snapshot Phase A was measured on, named by repro/phase_a.lock.json and required by scripts/reproduce_phase_a.sh for an exact rerun
